references.text: Jacob's blessing over Judah uses the same lion imagery to describe the tribe's strength and power, where the lion rises up and lies down.
Balaam's next oracle repeats the lion metaphor with nearly identical language, describing Israel as a lion that lies down and rises up.
The blessing over Benjamin describes the tribe as a wolf that devours prey and divides plunder, using similar imagery of eating prey.
Ezekiel uses the lion metaphor for Israel's princes who seize prey and devour people.
Isaiah describes the Lord as a lion roaring over its prey, with similar predator imagery.
Hosea describes God as a lion toward Ephraim and Judah, tearing apart so that no one can rescue.
Micah prophesies about Jacob's remnant among the nations as a lion among the beasts of the forest, trampling down and tearing to pieces.
Moses' blessing describes Gad as a lion that tears off arm and scalp, using similar imagery of the lion's strength.
